title: Efficient Human Pose Estimation Leveraging Advanced Techniques with MediaPipe

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (Related Work) — 'PoseNet Papandreou et al. (2018)' and reference list entry
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Papandreou et al. are not the authors of PoseNet; their works are 'Towards Accurate Multi-person Pose Estimation in the Wild' (CVPR 2017) and PersonLab (ECCV 2018). The reference also mislabels the year/venue ('2018 ... Proceedings of the CVPR'). The attribution of PoseNet to this reference is incorrect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Reference: Cao, Z. et al., 2019, OpenPose
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The OpenPose TPAMI paper is volume 43, no. 1, pp. 172–186, not 'IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 32, 172–186'. The volume number is wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction / Section 2 — 'MediaPipe ... offering robust, real-time, multi-person pose estimation capabilities' and 'designed for multi-person pose estimation on mobile devices'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: MediaPipe Pose (BlazePose) is a single-person pose tracker; it does not provide multi-person pose estimation. The paper's own experiments also only process a single human subject ('multiple key points on a human subject'), contradicting the multi-person claim.

predicted_errors.error_location: Angle computation equation in Section 3 (methodology) and the stage equation in the curl-counter section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: angle = arctan2(c_y−b_y, c_x−b_x) − arctan2(a_y−b_y, a_x−b_x) yields a signed value in (−360°, 360°); it is not constrained to [0°,180°]. Without taking the absolute value and folding values >180° (angle = 360 − angle), the thresholds 'angle > 160°' (down) and 'angle < 30°' (up) are not well defined and the counter logic can fail (e.g., a true 20° elbow flexion can be computed as −20° or 340°).

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 ('Experimental results showing the performance of the pose estimation system under different environmental conditions')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 1 is announced and described ('Table 1 summarizes the experimental data, indicating the system's performance across various conditions') but no table content, rows, or numbers are provided anywhere in the paper, so none of the claimed performance across conditions is verifiable.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusion ('20% increase in IoU', '~30% reduction in processing time') vs. Results section

predicted_errors.error_location: Methodology (performance indicators MSE and IoU) vs. Results/Conclusion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: MSE is declared a primary performance indicator (Eq. 1), but no MSE value or comparison is ever reported; only an unsupported IoU improvement is claimed. The stated evaluation protocol is not actually executed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract / Results discussion — 'Novel modifications', 'refined algorithms and the incorporation of advanced neural network architectures within the MediaPipe framework'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims novel algorithmic modifications and new neural network architectures inside MediaPipe, but the methodology only describes stock MediaPipe landmark extraction, an arctangent joint-angle formula, and a curl-counting heuristic. No architectural or algorithmic change is specified, so the claimed optimizations cannot be reproduced or verified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3 (Data collection) and Section 4 (comparison with 'baseline MediaPipe model' / 'traditional models')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: No dataset is named, no number of subjects/sequences/frames is given, no ground-truth annotation procedure is described, and no hardware or baseline configuration is specified. Yet the paper claims benchmarking against 'traditional models' and the baseline MediaPipe, and later discusses 'selection of datasets' bias for datasets never identified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Discussion — 'performance ... under challenging conditions like low light and partial occlusions, exhibits superior capabilities when compared to previous models documented in the literature'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: No experiment comparing the proposed system with any prior published model under low light or occlusion is reported; no numbers from literature are cited for comparison. The superiority claim is unsupported by any presented evidence.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 — 'often falter in complex real-world scenarios characterized by rapid movements, varying lighting conditions, and occlusions Li et al. (2021)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Li et al. (2021) is HybrIK, a hybrid analytical-neural inverse kinematics method for 3D pose and shape estimation; it is not a study documenting failures of pose estimators under varying lighting and occlusion, so the citation does not support the claim made.

predicted_errors.error_location: Reference list — Alam et al. (2022), Kim et al. (2023), Pavllo et al. (2019), Yurtsever & Eken (2022)
